texts.preamble: Jose Joseph vs State Of Kerala on 11 January, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Monday, The 11Th Day Of January 2016/21St Pousha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 2257 of 2005 ( ) --------------------------------- Crl.A 29/1997 Of The Additional Sessions Court-Ii, Mavelikkara Cc 198/1991 Of The Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Chengannur Revision Petitioners/Appellants 2 And 3: --------------------------------------- 1. Jose Joseph, Puthenparambil House, Veroor P.O., Vadakkekara, Changanachery. 2. St. Joseph'S Industries, Vadakkekara, Changanachry, Rep. By Sri.Jose Joseph, Puthenparambil House, Veroor P.O, Changanachery. By Advs.Sri.Mvs.Namboothiry Sri.Deepak Thomas Respondent/Respondent/Complainant/State: -------------------------------------- State Of Kerala, Rep. By The Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala, Ernakulam.
texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 17.9.1991 at about 10 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 6 packets of coriander powder, each packet having a weight of 100 grams each from the shop of the first accused. The second and the third accused persons were the manufacturers of the food item. After sampling as per law, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P12 report stating that the sample contained 7% of wheat starch and was therefore adulterated. After complying with the legal formalities, the complaint was filed before the court. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts. P1 to P22 were marked for the prosecution. DW1 and DW2 were examined and Exts.D1 to D4 were marked for the revision petitioners.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P12 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act . Therefore, Ext. P12 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case as adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Jose Joseph vs State Of Kerala on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179837007/ 2 A Division Bench of this Court in judgment dated 17-11-2015 in Crl.M.C. No. 417 of 2011 held that the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) is applicable to all cases.
